name: Verisk Analytics
description: Verisk sells data, predictive analytics, software and workflow tools to insurers, mainly in U.S. property and casualty insurance. Its products help insurers decide which risks to accept and how to price them (policy forms, rules, loss costs, geospatial and property data) and then handle claims (repair-cost estimating, fraud and injury analytics, catastrophe modelling). It reports one segment, Insurance. Most revenue is hosted subscriptions on one-to-five-year contracts billed in advance, with a smaller layer of transaction-priced and advisory work. Operating margin is about 44% and EBITDA margin about 54%.

employees.note: Approximately 8,000 employees worldwide; 57% in the U.S., 11% UK, 11% India.

businessLines.name: Underwriting & Rating (Insurance segment)
businessLines.how: Insurers pay annual or multi-year subscriptions (billed quarterly or annually in advance) for industry-standard policy forms, rules, loss costs, rating and property-risk data and tools, plus per-lookup transaction fees for items such as property-specific rating information.

businessLines.name: Claims (Insurance segment)
businessLines.how: Insurers and adjusters pay subscriptions and per-claim transaction fees for repair-cost estimating, claims investigation and fraud analytics, injury-claim analytics and catastrophe-loss tools used after a loss occurs.

brands.name: ISO (Insurance Services Office)
brands.note: The founding business (1971); the 10-K does not break out its revenue separately from the one Insurance segment.
